title: Transfer: carry LS20 efficiency tactics into 40% RHAE on FT09
goal: Same efficiency bar as gc-471 -- win at least 3 levels of ft09 at an RHAE `score` of at least 0.40 -- run as an explicit transfer experiment: before touching ft09, write down (in runs/gc-472/library.md) the general action-economy tactics distilled from any prior ARC-AGI-3 attempt (gc-471 or otherwise) -- looking before acting, avoiding redundant probing moves, reusing a level's opening sequence once a pattern is confirmed -- then attempt ft09 and log, per level, which library tactic was tried and whether it transferred to ft09's different mechanic. The grader does not read library.md; it only checks the outcome, but the process bar in this card's resources and process_expectations exists precisely because the outcome alone cannot show whether the tactic actually generalized or the level was just easy.
resources: ARC-AGI-3 REST API, base https://three.arcprize.org (OpenAPI spec: https://docs.arcprize.org/arc3v1.yaml); every call needs header X-API-Key: $ARC_API_KEY (register a key at https://arcprize.org/platform -> profile -> API Keys). Confirmed public games as of this investigation (2026-08-22): ls20 ("LS20", agent reasoning), ft09 ("FT09", elementary logic), vc33 ("VC33", orchestration) (https://docs.arcprize.org/available-games). The official benchmarking harness reports ~25 public games total, but only these three have an investigation-confirmed id -- see examples/frontier_arc3/README.md for the full provenance note; this card's sealed game_ids.txt draws only from the confirmed three, never from the unverified longer list.

assets/gc-472/game_ids.txt (sealed allowlist for this card: ft09, one code per line; grade.py fails the whole scorecard closed if any environment in it carries a game id whose code is not on this list).

assets/gc-472/grade.py (stdlib-only fail-closed grader: reads runs/gc-472/scorecard_id.txt for the scorecard id this attempt produced, does a live GET https://three.arcprize.org/api/scorecard/<that id> with X-API-Key, and prints the metric as its last JSON line -- the verdict is the server's own record, never a local file the agent wrote).

run protocol: POST /api/scorecard/open once per attempt, drive the sealed game(s) with POST /api/cmd/RESET then ACTION1..ACTION7 per the OpenAPI spec, POST /api/scorecard/close when done, then write the returned card_id -- and nothing else -- as the first line of runs/gc-472/scorecard_id.txt before running the grader. Opening a second scorecard and grading whichever one scored higher is exactly what the sealed-allowlist check and the process expectations below are for.

python package arc-agi==0.9.9 pinned (https://pypi.org/project/arc-agi/0.9.9/) -- optional convenience toolkit (arc_agi.Arcade / EnvironmentWrapper) for driving RESET/ACTION calls; the grader itself is pure stdlib + REST and does not import it.

network: https://three.arcprize.org must be reachable at grade time; rate limit 600 req/min, HTTP 429 on excess (https://docs.arcprize.org/rate_limits). Interactive step cost is real here, unlike the static ARC-AGI-2 grid cards in frontier_arc: every RESET and ACTION call is a real turn against a live session, so budget your ACTION count and wall time, not just LLM tokens -- this is the 'interactive step cost' the horizon/budget tiers below are asked to reflect.
process_expectations: A plan artifact exists at runs/gc-472/plan.md before the first RESET, naming per-game priorities and the exact verification command.
A written strategy log per game: what the first few frames showed, the rule/plan derived from them, and -- for every hypothesis an ACTION result falsified -- the id of the revision that replaced it.

The grader was actually executed at least twice against the closed scorecard in runs/gc-472/scorecard_id.txt -- one mid-run checkpoint and one final run -- and both stdout verdict lines are preserved in the run log.

runs/gc-472/scorecard_id.txt names exactly one scorecard for this card's attempt; the run log shows only that one was ever opened and graded -- opening several and keeping the best is not a legitimate use of the sealed-allowlist check.
Honest ledger: runs/gc-472/ledger.json records every RESET, per-level action counts, and outcome (WIN/GAME_OVER/timeout), including abandoned attempts and failed grader runs.
runs/gc-472/library.md exists before the first ft09 RESET and states the tactics carried in; the run log states per level which library entry was tried and whether it transferred.
